data.title: Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031
data.description:
(06:00 GMT) *Novartis Expects Sales to Grow 5% at Constant Currency Through 2031
(06:01 GMT) *Novartis Sees Core Operating Profit Margin on Track to Return to Above 40% by 2029
(06:02 GMT) *Novartis Raises Peak Sales Guidance for Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio
(06:02 GMT) *Novartis Had Previously Targeted Annual Sales Growth of 5%-6% Over 2025-30 Period
(06:03 GMT) *Novartis Sees Kesimpta Peak Annual Sales at $8B, Up From $6B Previously
(06:04 GMT) *Novartis: Scemblix Peak Sales Guidance Raised From $4B to $5B
(06:04 GMT) *Novartis: Leqvio Peak Sales Guidance Raised From $4B to $5B
(06:05 GMT) *Novartis Says It Now Has Nine In-Market Assets With Peak Sales Potential of $3B-$10B
(06:06 GMT) *Novartis: Drug Pipeline Expected to Support Sustained Mid-Single-Digit Growth Long Term
(06:24 GMT) Novartis Sees Sales Growth Through 2031

By Adria Calatayud

Novartis forecast steady sales growth through 2031, citing momentum from drugs already in the market and upcoming launches, and said medicines it has in the pipeline would help it sustain growth over the long term.

The Swiss drugmaker said Thursday that it expects annual sales growth of 5% from 2026 to 2031, excluding the effect of currency movements. It had previously forecast annual sales growth in the 5% to 6% range over the 2025-30 period.

Novartis raised its peak sales estimates for key drugs Kesimpta, Scemblix and Leqvio, saying this reinforces confidence in the company's midterm outlook.

The company said it now has nine in-market products with potential to generate annual peak sales of between $3 billion and $10 billion, as well as 10 in late-stage development that could bring in multibillion-dollar sales at their peak.

Novartis also said it is on track to return to a core operating profit margin above 40% by 2029, as previously indicated.

data.title: A2 Milk Cuts H1 Revenue View, Backs Outlook For H1 EBITDA Margin, FY27; Shares Down
data.description:
CANBERA (dpa-AFX) - a2 Milk Company Ltd. or a2MC (ACOPF, A2M.AX) on Thursday announced that it has trimmed revenue outlook for first half of fiscal 2027, amid the ongoing China Infant Milk Formula or IMF recovery efforts. Further, the firm maintained its outlook for first-half EBITDA margin as well as fiscal 2027.

At its Annual Meeting, the New Zealand-based dairy company also provided an update on its China IMF recovery plan.

In New Zealand, the shares traded 9.70 percent lower, and closed Thursday's trading at NZ$8.01.

Looking ahead for the first half, the company continues to project EBITDA margin to be materially down from last year. Meanwhile, revenues are now expected to be slightly lower year-over-year, while previous view was for revenue to be broadly in line with the prior year.

Further, for fiscal 2027, a2MC said it continues to expect revenue and EBITDA to grow in fiscal 2027, supported by increased contribution from product innovation and new markets, continued momentum in Other Nutritionals and Liquid Milk, and a2 Pokeno profitability improvement.

The firm still projects mid-single-digit percentage revenue growth and Underlying EBITDA margin of approximately 15 percent.

At this stage, the Company still expects total IMF sales to be broadly similar to fiscal 2026.

China label and English label are expected to gradually recover over the course of the new year, supported by the recent launches of two new China label products and the updated a2 Platinum product, and pending resolution of the China importation requirements currently impacting a2 Genesis.

The firm noted that IMF recovery will be supported by an increase in marketing, particularly in the first half. As a result, Group revenue and EBITDA are expected to be materially weighted to the second half of fiscal 2027.

The company previously expected China label to gradually recover over the course of fiscal 2027, and English label offtake momentum to improve during the first half, supported by an increase in marketing particularly in the first half.

The Company, as announced earlier, was impacted by shortfalls of China label IMF product that materially impacted in-market product availability during the fourth quarter. The issue necessitated a large proportion of existing users to switch to alternative brands, with the flow-on effects expected to impact IMF sales in fiscal 2027.

In addition, English label IMF offtake in the fourth quarter was indirectly impacted by the USA label IMF recall announced in May 2026.

Regarding the execution of its China IMF recovery plan, the company noted that so far, estimated China label offtake has recovered to around 50 percent of pre-supply chain disruption levels, up from around 40 percent in August 2026.

data.title: Time For Copper-Focused BHP to Show How It Can Grow — Analysis
data.description:
By Rhiannon Hoyle

ADELAIDE, Australia--A year ago, BHP Group abandoned a bid for Anglo American, reassuring investors it had plenty of options to produce more copper as global demand for the metal swells.

Now the world's most valuable miner needs to show it can deliver.

Copper has become a hot property as investors pour billions into building data centers, making electric vehicles and upgrading power grids. Copper prices hit a record high of $6.8035 per pound on Comex in September, although the market has been volatile lately as Nvidia's leadership turmoil and security concerns deal a blow to the artificial-intelligence trade.

On Monday, BHP begins a two-day investor tour of its Australian copper operations that analysts say could be the single biggest contributor to the company's growth in copper over the coming decade.

The visit to the operations, which are known collectively as Copper South Australia and comprise three mines, processing facilities and an exploration project, could be a chance to build investor confidence in the company's plans.

BHP has "set out an enticing copper growth story," helping its stock outperform many peers year to date, UBS said recently. The miner is betting the world's demand for copper will be reshaped by powerful long-term trends, including the AI boom.

But even BHP acknowledges that copper mines are harder to develop than before. Analysts expect its copper production will drop in the next two years as the business mines less copper-rich ore at pits in Chile.

"While BHP is a good operator, we see challenges with its copper growth," UBS said.

BHP has long wanted to transform its Australian assets, built from acquisitions in 2005 and more recently in 2023, into a business that ranks among the largest in the world.

However, those plans have been delayed for years by high costs and complex geology.

At the heart of Copper South Australia lies the mine and processing facilities of Olympic Dam, one of the world's biggest known deposits of copper, gold and uranium.

Back in 2012, BHP abandoned a proposed expansion that would have turned the underground mine there into a giant open pit for a cost that some analysts estimated to be close to $30 billion.

Helped by the 2023 takeover of copper miner Oz Minerals, BHP more recently developed a plan for a staged expansion of its smelting and refining capacity and its mines to create what it says could be a globally significant mine-to-metal copper province.

BHP aims to make a final investment decision on a major smelter and refinery expansion in 2027, with other possible projects to follow. RBC Capital Markets estimates a first phase of development--including the smelter and refinery project, and expansions at both its Olympic Dam and Carrapateena mines--to cost about $11.6 billion.

Importantly, BHP has improved the reliability of operations at Olympic Dam, which was for years beset by operational instability and external infrastructure constraints, weighing on returns, analysts say.

Last fiscal year, Olympic Dam recorded its highest copper production in more than two decades.

Still, investors are cautious about how quickly the miner can meet its goals.

BHP wants the Australian operations to produce about 500,000 metric tons of copper annually by 2035, up 56% on the 320,700 tons produced in the year through June. It is targeting annual production of up to 650,000 tons by 2040.

The market forecasts output of around 400,000 tons in 2035, 20% below the miner's target, according to Visible Alpha.

"Consensus does not yet have conviction in the production," said Bank of America.

Analysts say that could change once they get a closer look at BHP's plans for the operations. Investors will be seeking greater detail on costs, timing and obstacles to delivering the projects during the visit.

"Evidence of progress… should improve investors' confidence in the pathway," Citi said.

data.title: KKR Invests in India Renewables Business Run by Petronas-Backed Gentari
data.description:
By Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Investment firm KKR has made a minority investment in a renewable-energy platform in India run by Gentari, an entity established by Malaysia's national oil and gas company.

The investment will provide growth capital to support the renewables platform's continued expansion in India, KKR and Gentari said Thursday.

No terms were disclosed.

KKR has been investing in India's infrastructure sector for more than a decade, and has committed more than $27 billion to energy-transition and renewables infrastructure globally since 2011.

The deal with Gentari--part of Petronas Group--aims to capture the need for continued investment in India's energy infrastructure as demand for reliable power grows rapidly.

"We believe scaled platforms that can deliver increasingly sophisticated renewable energy solutions will have an important role to play in meeting that demand," said Hardik Shah, Asia-Pacific infrastructure partner at KKR.

Gentari's India platform has about 8 gigawatts of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable-energy capacity. Its portfolio spans solar, wind, hybrid and battery-energy storage solutions.

Gentari Group Chief Executive Sushil Purohit said that with KKR's support, it is well-positioned to keep scaling the business.

Following the investment, Gentari will retain strategic oversight and operational control of the platform, the companies said.

The tie-up comes on the heels of KKR's roughly $16 billion partnership with RWE investing in offshore-wind farms in the U.K.

data.title: Square Australia and NAB Team Up to Make Business Simpler
data.description:
Square Australia and National Australia Bank (NAB) are teaming up to make banking and payments simpler for Australian businesses and give them greater control over their cash flow.

For small businesses, including those in retail and hospitality, cash flow matters, margins matter and time matters. The partnership combines NAB’s business banking expertise with Square’s leading payments and business tools to make it easier for customers to manage the everyday work of running a business.

Initially, the partnership will provide eligible NAB customers using Square access to Square’s flexible transfer feature, giving them more control over when their available funds are sent to their NAB Business Transaction Account.

From February next year, businesses can set a close of day time for each day of the week, with Square initiating the transfer of their available funds to their NAB Business Transaction Account 15 minutes later.

NAB Group Executive Business and Private Banking Andrew Auerbach said the partnership reflected the bank’s ambition to keep supporting customers to make running their business easier.

“Many hospitality and retail businesses don’t operate nine to five,” Mr. Auerbach said.

“A restaurant might finish trading late at night and need to pay suppliers the next morning. A café might need to buy tomorrow’s produce, so their banking and payments need to work around how they do business.

“NAB already supports businesses of all shapes and sizes across Australia. We want to keep raising the bar by finding practical ways to make running them easier.

“These sound like small things, but they can make a big difference when you’re running a business. Flexible transfer is the first Square feature being made available through the partnership and we want to build on it.”

Block Global Partnerships Lead Morgan Kuntze said the partnership combined Square’s technology and understanding of sellers with NAB’s expertise in business banking.

“Square works with businesses every day, helping them take payments and manage the day-to-day work that sits behind making a sale,” Ms. Kuntze said.

“By partnering with NAB, we can connect that experience more closely with banking and find new ways to make managing money simpler for sellers.

“Flexible transfer is the first step. Sellers can set their close of day schedule around the way their business operates, and Square automatically initiates the transfer of their available funds.”

For Axil Coffee Roasters, which has grown from a single Hawthorn cafe to more than 16 locations and hundreds of wholesale partners, managing cash flow is part of the everyday reality of running a growing hospitality business.

“There’s no standard working day in hospitality,” said Axil Managing Director David Makin.

“Some of our venues open incredibly early, others trade later, and every day we’re managing staff, stock and suppliers across the business.

“Being able to set our transfer schedule around how we actually trade gives us another level of control over our cash flow.

“We need the flexibility. The more our banking and payments can fit around how the business actually operates, rather than the other way around, the better.”

Through the partnership, NAB and Square plan to build on flexible transfer by exploring further ways to connect banking and payments, simplify cash flow and make it easier for Australian businesses to operate and grow.

NAB has opened up the ability for businesses to express interest in the partnership ahead of the full launch in early 2027 - click here for more information.

Notes to editors:

  • NAB’s current standard settlement time is 9.30pm AEST daily.

  • Square’s flexible transfers require a linked and eligible NAB Business Transaction Account. The availability of funds in the linked bank account may be affected by NAB processing requirements.

  • Square applies transfer limits ranging from $5 to $50,000 AUD per day (new sellers are limited to $5,000 AUD per day until eligible for a higher limit). Flexible Transfers may not be available in limited circumstances beyond Square’s control, including where the linked bank account is not eligible for real-time payments or where there is downtime or delay affecting the New Payments Platform. Square’s Terms of Service apply.

About Square
Square helps businesses turn transactions into connections and businesses into neighbourhood favourites. In 2009, Square started with a simple invention — the first mobile card reader, which changed how the entire financial system thinks about small businesses. Square has since grown into a global business platform helping millions of sellers of all sizes participate and thrive in their communities. Whether independently run or a global chain, Square understands that sellers succeed when they have the freedom to focus on the experiences that keep customers coming back. From point of sale and payments to online commerce, staff management, cash flow tools, and more, Square brings together the tools sellers need to run and grow on one intelligent platform. For more information, visit squareup.com.

About NAB

At National Australia Bank (NAB) Group, our ambition is to be the most customer-centric company in Australia and New Zealand. More than 41,000 colleagues at the bank provide 10 million customers with secure, easy and reliable banking services. About 88% of the Group’s workforce are located in Australia and New Zealand, while others work in Asia, London, New York and Paris. NAB is proud to be Australia’s largest business lender. We stand by our customers, and they have our ongoing support.

data.title: PANW Stock Surges 8% Overnight: Palo Alto Networks CEO Sees ‘Hundreds Of Billions Of Dollars’ Opportunity In Open-Weight AI Models Security
data.description:
Key points:
  • CEO Nikesh Arora said open-weight AI models’ share of token usage has climbed from below 5% to over 60% in a year. 
  • Palo Alto Networks has bought Applied Compute for $4.5 billion to strengthen its AI security business. 
  • The company plans to develop over 35 AI-powered security applications and deliver sovereign open-weight models. 

Palo Alto Networks (PANW) stock jumped 8% overnight after a third-quarter (Q3) earnings beat, as CEO Nikesh Arora highlighted a market worth billions for securing open-weight AI models. Speaking on the Q3 earnings call, Arora outlined the company's Applied Compute acquisition, which aims to expand enterprise AI security and bring in $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by fiscal 2029.

Palo Alto Networks’ stock is on track for a second straight weekly gain.

PANW CEO Sees Open Weight AI Models Gaining Enterprise Interest

Arora said during the Q3 earnings call that businesses are opting for AI models that give them greater ownership and control over their technology. Open-weight models have gained traction, making up more than 60% of token usage, compared with less than 5% a year earlier.

“When organizations put AI at the center of their operations, they want to retain control of their proprietary data, institutional judgment and competitive edge inside their own 4 walls. We expect a future with a serving opportunity in the hundreds of billions of dollars when enterprise applications are driven by open weight and open source adoption.”

Applied Compute To Support Palo Alto Networks’ AI Security Expansion

To address the enormous security opportunity, Arora said Palo Alto Networks examined potential partners across the AI industry before selecting Applied Compute, citing its engineering capabilities and experience in developing open-weight models through post-training. Palo Alto Networks agreed to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at $4.5 billion.

The Palo Alto-Applied Compute deal will focus on two things. Networks plans to integrate AI into its existing cybersecurity products, developing more than 35 specialized applications that will help customers counter AI-led threats with AI-driven defenses.

The second focus will be developing and delivering secure, sovereign versions of open-weight models for enterprise customers. “To support our efforts, we plan to build out a diversified global influence capability of north of 100-plus megawatts over the next 3 to 5 years,” Arora said.

“This will be supported by a modest CapEx commitment at least – of less than $3 billion through fiscal 2030, representing approximately half a year of our annual free cash flow.”

PANW Stock: Retail Stance

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock improved to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘bullish’ territory. The stock recorded an 884% surge in message volume over the past 24 hours.

A user said, “Applied Compute acquisition to bolster PANW’s enterprise capabilities in open-weight AI models.”

Another user said, “$PANW agreed to pay $4.5B in stock for Applied Compute, which helps companies customize and run AI models. That’s a pretty big bet that the folks who buy their cybersecurity will also trust them to help run the models. I’d like to see how many customers sign up for both.”

PANW stock has gained 84% year-to-date.

data.title: Asian stocks diverge on soft Australian employment and Anthropic IPO focus
data.description:
Asian equity markets traded mixed on Thursday as investors weighed fresh economic data across Japan and Australia, monetary policy commentary from the Bank of Japan, and the upcoming Wall Street debut of Anthropic.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 0.70% to 59,450 level, with the Japanese yen traded around 159.4. South Korea’s benchmark KOSPI rose 0.55% to around 5,095.30. Meanwhile, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index () fell 2.19%, to around 22,790.00, and mainland China’s Shanghai Composite () fell 0.69% to 3,563.56, while the Shenzhen Component fell 0.67% to 10,586. The offshore yuan steadied around 6.66 per dollar. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 () fell 1.04%, to 8,730.40. The Australian dollar slipped below $0.67 to its lowest level since December, wiping out all of its 2026 gains, as traders increased bets that the Reserve Bank of Australia will pivot toward interest rate cuts next year.

Australia’s October’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate jumped to 4.9% from 4.7% and total employment dropped by 43,500 to a five-month low of 14.74 million, fueling bets on Reserve Bank of Australia rate cuts next year.

Japan’s core machinery orders slipped 0.3% M/M to JPY 1,066.2B in September, beating forecasts for a 0.5% decline. Meanwhile, Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda told a parliamentary committee that underlying inflation must remain anchored around 2% and reiterated that the central bank will continue raising interest rates as economic and price conditions warrant.

In commodities and crypto, gold prices fell to around $3,700 an ounce, while crude oil prices held around $83 per barrel. Bitcoin slid toward $62,000 on Wednesday, reaching its lowest level since mid-July, as a hawkish US rate outlook, weaker risk appetite and crypto-specific selling weighed on demand.

Wall Street closed mixed on Wednesday after Nvidia erased its post-earnings rally, sparking a broader rotation away from AI stocks. U.S. stock futures ticked higher on Thursday ahead of Anthropic’s market debut, after the AI company priced its IPO above its initial target range on strong investor demand.

data.title: Sarvam sells DeepSeek access while pursuing sovereign AI models
data.description:
Sarvam has begun selling access to DeepSeek and other Chinese AI models, triggering an online backlash over its role as one of the main proponents of the country’s AI independence.

This week, Sarvam unveiled Token Factory, an inference platform offering multiple AI models via a single API interface, hosted on local computing infrastructure. Its catalog includes Sarvam’s own model, but also open-weight systems from Chinese AI labs DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and Z.AI Co.

Sarvam, valued at $1.5 billion in April, is the poster child for India’s push to create AI services tailored to the languages and cultures of the world’s most populous country. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government has made a forceful case that countries beyond the US and China need to control their own destiny with the emerging technology.

The controversy stems from Sarvam’s history. It built its frontier model on the backing of the government’s IndiaAI Mission, and was one of the first local startups to be given subsidized compute.

“We haven’t changed our motto. We continue to build AI models for India.

data.title: Bitcoin Bear Market Looks Shallow So Far — Market Talk
data.description: Bitcoin's drawdown cycle looks shallow so far, says digital-asset banking group Sygnum. The correction is contained against falls of more than 70% in previous cycles, Sygnum says in a report. By contrast, the drawdown from the latest high in October 2025 to the current bottom is roughly 54%. If Bitcoin doesn't fall below the June/July low this cycle, it would be the shallowest of any bear market to date. While it's too early to say whether the cycle has run its course, the asset class still seems to be entering 2027 with lower structural volatility, stronger fundamentals and clearer, if still incomplete, regulation, says CIO Fabian Dori. Bitcoin gains 1.8% but stays around three-month lows at $63,428. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)

data.title: London copper ticks higher from seven-month trough
data.description:
London copper prices nudged higher on Thursday after hitting their weakest level in seven months the previous session, while Shanghai copper prices continued to fall.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 0.8% to $12,562.50 a metric ton by 0605 GMT after hitting its lowest level since April 7 in the previous session. Wednesday's percentage drop in copper, used in the power and construction sectors, was its biggest one-day decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump was rolling out global tariffs.

The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SCFv1) fell 4.7% to 95,130 yuan ($14,270.71) a ton.

"The current move in LME copper prices looks more like relief than a decisive turn. The sharp retreat was driven by a buoyant US dollar and growing question marks over the pace of the AI data-center buildout, where copper is a key input in the infrastructure," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

"The main factors to watch remain the path of the dollar, any further signals on AI-related capital spending, and Chinese demand indicators."

The dollar hovered near a 19-month high after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments pointed to further US rate hikes. A stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated metals more expensive for holders of other currencies, while higher interest rates can weigh on growth-sensitive commodities such as copper by slowing economic activity.

Asian stocks slid as sentiment remained fragile ahead of an eagerly awaited market debut from Anthropic after the Claude chatbot maker scored the biggest IPO ever.

LME aluminium rose 1% after hitting a near one-year low on Tuesday and SHFE aluminium (SAFv1) fell 1.5%.

"Aluminium prices fell as supply improved and demand softened, with Middle East losses partly offset by strong production in China and ramping supply in Indonesia, while strong Chinese exports are making up for lower shipments from the Middle East," analysts at ANZ said in a note.

Among other LME metals, zinc firmed 1.3%, lead fell 0.1%, nickel eased 0.4% and tin lost 1.8%.

On the SHFE, zinc (SZNv1) declined 3%, lead (SPBv1) lost 0.7%, nickel (SNIv1) slipped 3.4% and tin (SSNv1) dipped 4.2%.

data.title: South Korean Tourism Stocks Rally on Hopes for Expanded China Trade Pact
data.description:
By Kwanwoo Jun

South Korean tourism stocks rallied Thursday on hopes that an expanded free-trade agreement between Seoul and Beijing would boost Chinese visitor arrivals.

China and South Korea earlier this week reached a deal to broaden the scope of their 2015 FTA to include sectors such as tourism, entertainment and investment services, wrapping up years of negotiations, according to President Lee Jae Myung's office in Seoul.

The deal, announced Wednesday after a bilateral summit between Lee and his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, China, allows South Korean travel agencies to organize outbound travel from 23 regions in China, according to South Korea's trade ministry.

In Seoul trading Thursday, travel company Hanatour Service jumped as much as 28%, while budget airline Jeju Air climbed up to 25%. Hotel Shilla, which operates hotels and duty-free shops, rose as much as 13%.

"The expansion of channels to attract Chinese tourists to South Korea is expected to further boost passenger demand on China routes," Hanwha Investment & Securities analyst Park Su-young said after the deal was reached.

The aviation, entertainment and leisure industries stand to gain from the latest Korea-China pact, with aviation likely to be the biggest beneficiary, she wrote in a research note.

Hana Securities analyst Dohyun Ahn viewed Jeju Air as a key beneficiary of the expanded FTA, citing the company's greater exposure to the Chinese market than any other South Korean low-cost carrier.

Routes to mainland China account for 8% of the South Korean budget airline's revenue, and that share could increase further, Ahn said.

In a statement on Wednesday's expanded deal, President Lee's office said South Korea and China should continue immigration measures to facilitate travel between the two countries to help boost bilateral people-to-people exchanges.

The office expects the number of people traveling between the two countries to reach 10 million this year and hopes it will eventually return to the 13 million recorded in 2016.

Exchanges have been constrained since Beijing allegedly restricted Chinese group tours to South Korea following Seoul's decision in 2016 to deploy a U.S. missile-defense system despite Chinese protests. Beijing has denied imposing a ban.

Write to Kwanwoo Jun at kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com

data.title: UniCredit and Germany reach broad agreement on Commerzbank takeover
data.description:
Key points:
  • Major development in two-year takeover battle
  • Merged bank's German headquarters to remain in Frankfurt as listed entity
  • Germany drops demand to name two Commerzbank supervisory board members
  • UniCredit pledges to add German nationals to its board of directors

By Holger Hansen

UniCredit and Germany have reached agreement on the big sticking points in the Italian bank's takeover of Commerzbank, a major development in the two-year battle for control of the German lender.

The agreement, laid out in a letter from UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel to German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil as well as a separate statement to Reuters from the German minister, states that the merged bank's German headquarters will remain in Frankfurt as a listed entity, a key German demand.

But Germany has given up its insistence on naming two supervisory board members to Commerzbank , in a concession to UniCredit.

A combination of UniCredit and Commerzbank would create a bank with more than €1.3 trillion ($1.4 trillion) in assets across two of the euro zone's ​largest economies in one of the most significant cross-border European banking deals in years.

In the letter dated November 18 and seen by Reuters, Orcel said he was "prepared to commit" to a series of binding principles and thanked Klingbeil for discussions "which have allowed us to find common ground."

UniCredit also pledged to put German nationals on UniCredit's board of directors.

Klingbeil, in his statement to Reuters, said Germany "supports a swift process and an orderly transition of control."

"We have reached common ground and UniCredit has made clear commitments to Germany as a business location, to the rights of Commerzbank employees and to a continued constructive dialogue with the works council in the further process," Klingbeil said, referring to a body of elected employee representatives.

GERMAN GOVERNMENT STAKE

Orcel pounced on Commerzbank in 2024, catching the lender and the government off guard by discreetly building up a holding. Commerzbank and Berlin tried to prevent the takeover, ​but gave in after UniCredit amassed a stake nearing ​50%.

Commerzbank employees have long been against a deal, in part due to Orcel's stated plans to cut jobs in Germany.

A key representative of Commerzbank's workforce said on Thursday that he welcomed the agreement for its commitment to Frankfurt as German headquarters, but warned that current employee contracts remain valid.

"If those agreements are respected as announced, there may not be years of confrontation ahead," said Sascha Uebel, head of Commerzbank's works council.

"Ultimately, it is now in Andrea Orcel's hands how we, as employees, will receive him here," he told Reuters.

The German government holds a 13.3% stake in Commerzbank following a bailout during the global financial crisis.

The sale of the federal government's stake remains an open question. Orcel's letter said UniCredit's agreements "set the basis for the disposal of the government's stake", but Klingbeil's statement contains no commitment to sell.

Klingbeil ​and Orcel met in September on the Italian bank's hostile €45 billion approach. Both called the talks "constructive" but differences remained.

Since then, the European Central Bank, the European Commission and the US Federal Reserve have given a green light to a deal, clearing regulatory hurdles.

Earlier this month, Commerzbank said that it was "convinced" a deal between the two ‌banks could create value, in a markedly more bullish stance on a potential tie-up it had long resisted.

($1 = 0.9115 euros)

data.title: Polish insurer PZU's third-quarter profit falls 28% on weather, motor claims
data.description:
Polish insurer PZU reported a 28% fall in its quarterly profit on Thursday, compared with a strong year-ago period, slightly missing market forecasts as hail damage, large claims and motor insurance price competition hit its mass-market non-life business.

Price competition has returned to Polish motor liability insurance since 2025, and premium increases are too small to significantly lift profitability as claims costs climb, PZU said.

  • Third-quarter net profit was 1.44 billion zlotys ($358 million) versus 1.46 billion zlotys expected by analysts in a company-compiled consensus

  • Non-motor policies accounted for more than half of the mass-market division's profit decline, while the motor business's own-damage cover swung to a loss

  • Operating profit in the Polish life insurance unit rose 16%, partly offsetting the decline, as claims came in below expectations due to lower mortality

  • Profit from PZU's stakes in Pekao and Alior fell 21%, affected by lower interest rates and a rise in bank corporate tax

  • The government has effectively abandoned the plan for Pekao to take over PZU and is instead considering a holding structure within the insurer, Business Insider Polska reported last week, citing State Assets Minister Wojciech Balczun

($1 = 4.0246 zlotys)

data.title: US dollar hits 19-month peak, Aussie drops after soft jobs data
data.description:
Key points:
  • Aussie drops to 10-month low after employment falls for second month
  • Dollar supported as Fed minutes, Waller comments point to more hikes
  • Investors eye Anthropic's blockbuster debut amid AI stock volatility

The US dollar climbed to a fresh 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Fed official pointed to further interest rate hikes, while the Aussie dollar slipped to a 10-month low after soft jobs data.

A broadly stronger US unit pressured the euro to near its lowest since April 2025, last trading at $1.0963, while sterling eased to a one-month low at $1.3117. The yen eased against the dollar at 159.56, hovering around the closely watched 160 level.

The dollar index edged up 0.1% at 103.97, its highest level since April 2025.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller reinforced that tone, saying the central bank should either raise rates by 50 basis points in December or signal faster hikes in 2027.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the dollar supported," OCBC analysts said, adding that a deeper downgrade to expectations for AI capital expenditure would challenge that support by pushing down US real yields and weakening equity inflows.

Chip bellwether Nvidia <NVDA.O> fell overnight even after beating on revenue and guidance amid uncertainties caused by co-founder Jensen Huang's sudden departure as CEO last week following his admission of extramarital affairs.

Investors are bracing for the stock market debut of Anthropic later on Thursday as a test for AI sentiment.

FALLING YIELDS AND OIL PRICES

Treasury yields have fallen despite the dollar's strength. The 10-year yield fell to 5.05%, a one-week low, after easing about 4 basis points overnight following a solid 20-year auction. Yields move inversely to bond prices.

"Falling oil prices helped ease some inflation concerns, while weakness in US equities and worries about economic growth may have encouraged some safe-haven buying in Treasuries," said Dilin Wu, a research strategist at Pepperstone, adding that the dollar's performance will depend on how its interest rate advantage and safe-haven demand evolve.

Oil prices steadied on Thursday after losses in the prior session as expectations for a market surplus outweighed lingering worries about Middle East supply amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures were trading up 5 cents, or 0.05%, at $92 a barrel.

Gold stabilised at $3,729 an ounce after a sharp selloff overnight on hawkish Fed signals.

The Swiss franc weakened 0.1% to 0.8435 per the US dollar. New Zealand's kiwi firmed 0.1% at $0.5496.

The Aussie dropped as low as $0.6662 for the first time since January. Australia's employment fell for a second straight month in October and the jobless rate climbed to a five-year high, bolstering the view that rates have likely peaked.

Following the data, UBS economist George Tharenou brought forward his forecast for the first Reserve Bank of Australia rate cut to August from November of next year, and extended the easing cycle to three cuts from two, citing elevated inflation and a deterioration in the labour and housing markets.

data.title: Loading ... Claude and GTA VI
data.description:
Key points:
  • EuroSTOXX50 futures up 0.4%
  • Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq
  • Nasdaq futures rise

LOADING ... CLAUDE AND GTA VI

A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee

The latest test of how investors feel about the AI trade is here as Claude chatbot maker Anthropic gets ready for its market debut after clinching an eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation in the biggest-ever initial public offering.

Anthropic is the first major frontier AI model developer to go public and priced its IPO at $83 apiece, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Investors say demand is robust for the offering, suggesting a strong opening day, though Asian equities are not basking in the afterglow. Worries about AI profitability and the massive debt-fuelled spending to build related infrastructure have dented sentiment for weeks and Thursday was no different in Asia.

US stock futures, though, pointed higher on the IPO pricing while European stocks were set for a strong opening, suggesting Asia's place as the epicentre of the AI boom has meant it is also feeling the pain much more.

Taiwan's stock market is where most of the action is this week, with the benchmark index TWSE:TAIEX down 3.4%, on pace for a weekly decline of 11%. South Korea's KOSPI was flat, set for a 4% weekly fall.

Hawkish comments from the Federal Reserve also cast a shadow over Asian markets, with traders bracing for a hike next month. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action." Traders are pricing in a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

That left the dollar standing tall at an 18-month high against major rivals. The yen remains perilously close to the 160-per-dollar mark, leaving traders jittery about intervention. The Asian currency is down 1.8% so far in 2026 as authorities in Tokyo stepped in to support the yen in several bouts of intervention earlier this year.

Anthropic's debut is not the only eagerly awaited event on Thursday, with "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolling out across the globe after 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs. Early reviews for the game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, are euphoric.

Key developments that could influence markets on Thursday:

Anthropic market debut, Walmart earnings, GTA VI debut
